just: one command for every task in a project

just is a command runner: a file called Justfile holds named recipes, and just name runs one. It looks like make, without the build-system baggage. For a data project it solves a simple problem: how do I run, test and check this thing, and will I remember in three months?

A typical project Justfile

default:
    @just --list

check:
    ruff check --fix
    ruff format
    pyright

test:
    uv run pytest

run *args:
    uv run python -m project {{args}}

Every project gets the same names (check, test, run), so my fingers do not need to know which project I am in. The recipes also document how things are run, for me and for the coding agents that work in the repository.

Parameters and defaults

Recipes take arguments with default values, which is what turns small scripts into tools. A recipe of mine that sends a file to another computer is declared as push force="false", and just push force=true overrides the safety check.

A global Justfile for the things I do everywhere

just -g runs recipes from a Justfile in my dotfiles. It is organised in modules, one file per topic, and the module name becomes the prefix:

mod git    "~/dotfiles/just/git.just"
mod watch  "~/dotfiles/just/watch.just"
mod scp    "~/dotfiles/just/scp.just"
mod vpn    "~/dotfiles/just/vpn.just"

So just -g scp push asks which of my computers I mean, lets me pick the file with a fuzzy finder and copies it over. The [no-cd] attribute keeps such a recipe in the directory I called it from, instead of jumping to the Justfile's folder.

Recipes for agents

I also keep launchers there for coding agents with a strict policy, for example a recipe that starts the agent so that it must show a diff and wait for my approval before touching a file. One word to start the agent in the mode I want, instead of a flag I would forget.

Find recipes with a fuzzy finder

I rarely type recipe names. A television channel lists the recipes of the local and the global Justfile with a preview of each one and runs the chosen one with a key. More in the post about tv.
